headline: Highest risk is data leakage: gpt-researcher’s broad egress and file access can expose local documents if paired with the read-only awesome-list workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no ingestion path; B can read files and parse web/MCP content, so only a manual bridge or copied content could carry prompt injection from A to B. The pairwise pathway is weak and not default, but B’s permissive parsers make copied content risky.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-derived text into B’s research inputs, THEN prompt injection becomes possible.
IF B ingests A content from a shared file or MCP source, THEN malicious instructions in that content can influence B.
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting untrusted A-derived text into B.
Strip instructions from any A-generated text before feeding B.
Use a read-only staging folder for A outputs.
Disable MCP sources that are not provenance-tagged.
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks before B parses external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B reads local documents and sends queries/reports through broad networked APIs. If A and B share a workspace, B can ingest local files and exfiltrate their contents to third-party services by default.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem workspace, THEN B can read A-produced files.
IF B processes local documents containing sensitive material, THEN those contents can be sent to external APIs.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Do not place sensitive files in B’s input folder.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
Run B with a dummy dataset first.
requires-engineering: restrict B’s outbound destinations and redact file contents before upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, while B supports subprocesses, package installs, and multiple instances. There is no overlapping mutable resource shown, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely unless an operator adds a shared workspace or shared credentials.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, THEN file-level conflicts can occur.
IF B instances share the same mutable research workspace, THEN concurrent edits can collide.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent B runs on the same project folder.
Do not let B install packages into a shared environment.
Snapshot the workspace before running B.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an informational awesome-list and B is a planner/execution/publisher research agent. If B treats A’s curated output as authoritative, errors or stale recommendations from A can cascade into B’s reports or actions without verification.
conditions: IF B uses A’s list entries as factual sources without independent verification, THEN incorrect claims can propagate.
IF B publishes a report based on A-derived references, THEN downstream outputs may inherit A’s errors.
mitigations: Require source verification before publication.
Mark A as a directory, not an authority.
Cross-check A entries against primary sources.
Add a human review step for any A-derived claim.
requires-engineering: enforce citation validation in B’s publisher stage.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. A touches no data classes and B handles local documents plus API keys, so the main compliance concern is generic retention/logging exposure rather than a proven jurisdictional breach.
conditions: IF regulated documents are fed into B, THEN external API logging/retention may create compliance obligations.
IF B is used with secrets or customer data, THEN retention controls must be verified.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data in B until policies are reviewed.
Remove secrets from test runs.
Check vendor retention settings before use.
Document data flows for any production deployment.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the workflow.
